<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company&#146;s purpose shall be to perform, on its own, through third parties or in association with third parties, the survey, exploration and
exploitation of liquid and/or gaseous hydrocarbon fields and other minerals, as well as the industrialization, transportation and commercialization of these products and their direct and indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT>
including petrochemical products, chemical products, whether derived from hydrocarbons or not, and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-fossil</FONT> fuels, biofuels and their components, as well as the generation of electrical energy through the
use of hydrocarbons, to which effect it may manufacture, use, purchase, sell, exchange, import or export them. It shall also be the Company&#146;s purpose the rendering, on its own, through a controlled company or in association with third parties,
of telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing,
commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its
object. To better achieve these purposes, it may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim
consolidated financial statements of the Company for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim financial reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual
consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;) presented in U.S. dollars and in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are unaudited. The
Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30,
2024, does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 18. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional
currency </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The consolidated financial statements used by YPF for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes in Argentina are those in pesos and filed with the
CNV and approved by the Board of Directors and authorized to be issued on November&nbsp;7, 2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group maintains share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 37 of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements
and Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#147;Share-based payment&#148;. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service
based on the Group&#146;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#147;Share-based benefit plans&#148; account in the statement of
changes in shareholders&#146; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the grant conditions specified under the respective benefit plan.
</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:50pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January&nbsp;1, 2024 </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of September&nbsp;30, 2024, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and
interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024, whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for
issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into 3 defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing, and
include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 19 &#147;Subsidiaries without public accountability: Disclosures&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 19 with the objective of allowing the option to apply simplified disclosure requirements in the financial statements of
subsidiaries without public accountability and with a parent company, ultimate or intermediate, that prepares consolidated financial statements for public use in accordance with IFRS. Its application is optional for fiscal years beginning on or
after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">President&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;&#8195; </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Amendments to IFRS 9 &#147;Financial instruments&#148; and IFRS 7 &#147;Financial instruments: Disclosures&#148; -
Amendments to the classification and measurement of financial instruments </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued amendments to IFRS 9 and
IFRS 7 related to certain issues regarding the classification and measurement requirements of IFRS 9 and the disclosure requirements of IFRS 7, which are applicable for periods beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2026: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

</P></TD></TR></TABLE>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of
preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key sources of uncertainty
about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed in Note
2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other information corresponding to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023, are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated
financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements, considering the changes in comparative figures as mentioned in Note 6. Amounts corresponding to the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2023,
presented in these financial statements for comparison purposes correspond to the functional currency of the company according to IAS 21 (see Note 2.b)). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, from this fiscal year, the Group has made a change in the presentation of the items in the &#147;Financial results, net&#148; line item in
the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 29). This change is intended to provide more relevant and detailed information on the origin of financial results and the effects of transactions or conditions that affect the financial situation,
financial performance, and cash flows of the Group such as interests and exchange differences generated by loans, among others; and improve the comparability of the Group&#146;s financial statements with its peers. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Liquidity risk management </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the
Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Notes 17 and 33. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quaterly basis. As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, the Group is in compliace with its covenants. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_12"></A>6.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented consistently with the manner of reporting the information
used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segment structure is organized as
follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of fields and production of crude oil
and natural gas. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the crude oil produced to the Downstream business
segment; and (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the natural gas produced and the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly
included in Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. In addition, the comparative information for fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023, has been restated. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Downstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products;
(ii)&nbsp;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&nbsp;commercialization of refined
and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&nbsp;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&nbsp;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="font-size:70pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:48pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD VALIGN="top" COLSPAN="5"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>6.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION (cont.) </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical
products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro,
Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs
related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of: (i)&nbsp;crude oil from the Upstream business segment and third parties; (ii)&nbsp;natural gasoline and natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial
complexes from the Gas and Power business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;propane and butane to be commercialized from the Gas and Power business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Gas and Power </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Gas and Power business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas transportation to third parties and the Downstream
business segment and its commercialization; (ii)&nbsp;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&nbsp;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained
in plant for the separation and fractionation of natural gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&nbsp;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (v)&nbsp;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&nbsp;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and
natural gasoline; (ii)&nbsp;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&nbsp;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business
segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of natural gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant
from the Upstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Central Administration and Others </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It covers other activities performed by the Group not falling under the business segments mentioned above and which are not reporting
business segments, mainly comprising corporate administrative expenses and assets and construction activities. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024,
certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly included in Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. In addition, the comparative information for
fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023, has been restated. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Sales between business segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the
Group, which generally seek to approximate domestic market prices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Operating profit or loss and assets of each business segment have been determined
after consolidation adjustments. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group capitalizes the financial cost of loans as part of the cost of the property, plant and
equipment. For the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the rate of capitalization was 7.44% and 8.26%, respectively, and the amount capitalized amounted to 5 and 14, respectively. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>17. PROVISIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Provisions are described in Note 16 to the annual consolidated financial statements. Updates for the
nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>17.a) Provision for lawsuits and contingencies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Environmental claims</U> </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>La Plata </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;29, 2024 the Court of Appeals confirmed the obligation to cease and remedy the environmental damage determined in the first instance. The <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">co-defendants</FONT> filed an extraordinary appeal to the CSJN and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, such appeal is pending resolution. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_24"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to
IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria
that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to
property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in
accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group considers
having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of
September&nbsp;30, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 416. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the nine-month period ending
September&nbsp;30, 2024 is a profit of 987. The amount accrued for the nine-month periods ending September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE CELLSPACING="0" CELLPADDING="0" WIDTH="90%" BORDER="0" STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:7pt">

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_27"></A>21. LEASE LIABILITIES </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The
evolution of the Group&#146;s leases liabilities for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023, are as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_37"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,922 and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares
of common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the
affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the
voluntary dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the
outstanding Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 1,244 million); (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 36 million) to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972&nbsp;million of
pesos (US$ 4,236 million) to constitute a reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the Company
has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_38"></A>32. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>33. CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs and the Republic completed their briefing on the turnover motion on July&nbsp;8, 2024. The
District Court may, but is not required to, hold oral argument prior to rendering a decision on the turnover motion. Furthermore, the District Court&#146;s decision on the turnover motion may be appealed by Plaintiffs or the Republic in accordance
with applicable procedural rules. YPF is not a party to the turnover motion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs are also seeking discovery of documents from YPF related to
their theory that YPF could be an &#147;alter ego&#148; of the Republic. YPF denies that it is an <I>alter ego</I> and objected to Plaintiffs&#146; document requests. On May&nbsp;28, 2024, the District Court ordered YPF to produce documents in
response to Plaintiffs&#146; discovery requests. To date, Plaintiffs have not requested that the District Court find that YPF is an <I>alter ego</I> of the Republic, and the District Court&#146;s order on discovery is not a ruling accepting
Plaintiffs&#146; <I>alter ego</I> theory. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;12, 2024, YPF filed a brief requesting that the District Court permanently enjoin
Plaintiffs from pursuing recovery from YPF in connection with their September&nbsp;15, 2023 final judgment against the Republic, arguing that Plaintiffs&#146; alter ego theory is barred under the doctrine of res judicata. Plaintiffs filed their
opposition and YPF filed its reply. On August&nbsp;29, 2024, the District Court adjourned the oral argument initially scheduled for September&nbsp;3, 2024, without setting a new date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF will continue to defend itself in accordance with the applicable legal procedures and available defenses. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company will continue to reassess the status of the litigation and its possible impact on the results and financial situation of the Group, as
needed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_40"></A>34. CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS </B></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_41"></A>35. MAIN REGULATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.a.1) Hydrocarbons Law </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Hydrocarbons Law, as described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that international trade of hydrocarbons will be free, according to the terms and conditions established by
the PEN. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that exploration permit holders and/or exploitation concessionaires, refiners and/or marketers may freely
export hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives, subject to the SE&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-objection.</FONT> The effective exercise of this right will be subject to regulations issued by the PEN, which, among other aspects, must
consider: (i)&nbsp;the usual requirements related to the access to technically proven resources; and (ii)&nbsp;that the eventual objection of the SE may only be formulated within 30 days of being informed of the exports to be made, and must be based
on technical or economic reasons related to the security of supply. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:3pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On 5&nbsp;June 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;93/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas
prices at the PIST in U.S. dollars corresponding to the awarded volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions from June 2024 and leaves without effect the instruction to
ENARGAS to issue tariff schemes that reflect on a monthly basis the variation of the exchange rate of the prices of natural gas to be transferred to the tariff schemes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On November&nbsp;1, 2024, Resolution No.&nbsp;18/2024 of the Secretariat of Mining and Energy Coordination was published in the BO, which modify SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;93/2024 approving the natural gas prices at the PIST in U.S. dollars corresponding to the awarded volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions from
November 2024. See Note 35.c.2). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Bottle-to</FONT> Bottle Program</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;19, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;216/2024 was published in the BO, which resolved to eliminate the maximum prices applicable set for
bottled LPG for residential use and replace them with a reference price system (without ceiling). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.e) Investment incentive programs </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Large Investment Incentive Regime (&#147;RIGI&#148;) </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Bases Law (see Note 35.j)) created the RIGI, regulated by Decree No.&nbsp;749/2024 published in the BO on August&nbsp;23, 2024, General Resolution
No.&nbsp;1,074/2024 of the Ministry of Economy published in the BO on October&nbsp;22, 2024 and AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,590/2024 published in the BO on October&nbsp;23, 2024, which is intended to encourage large investments with tax,
customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights. This regime seeks to encourage investments, promote economic development, create employment and strengthen local production chains. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The RIGI is aimed at investment projects in the forestry industry, tourism, infrastructure, mining, technology, iron and steel, energy and oil and gas
sectors, with a minimum investment per sector or subsector or productive stage equal to or greater than a range between US$ 200,000,000 up to US$ 900,000,000 in computable assets, as established by the application authority. Interested parties have
2 years to adhere to the RIGI, submitting and obtaining the approval of an investment plan by the application authority. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The benefits of the RIGI
include a 25% income tax rate, accelerated amortization of investments, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-expirable</FONT> tax loss carryforwards, indexing tax losses by the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#147;IPIM&#148;) published by the
INDEC, and exemptions from import and export duties, among others. In addition, foreign exchange incentives are established, such as the free availability of foreign currency on a staggered basis obtained from exports and certain flexibility related
to financing. The RIGI guarantees tax, customs and foreign exchange regulatory stability for 30 years from accession, protecting investment projects from more burdensome legislative changes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.f) Tax regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework
described in Note 35.e) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tax for an Inclusive and Solidary Argentina (&#147;PAIS Tax&#148;, by its acronym in Spanish)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;2, 2024, Decree No.&nbsp;777/2024 was published in the BO, which reduced to 7.5% the rate applied to foreign currency purchases for
contracting, abroad or in the country by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-residents,</FONT> freight services and other transport services for the import or export of goods and for the import of goods, except for those mentioned in section 2
paragraph e) of Decree No.&nbsp;377/2023 and its corresponding regulations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.g) Custom regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.f) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,520/2024 was published in the BO, which extend,
until December&nbsp;31, 2024, the provisions established of AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,339/2023, as amended (see Note 35.f.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.h) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility
of applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19, 2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average
life of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior
approval process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs
simultaneously with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new debt is greater than the average remaining life of the
anticipated debt; and (iii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;28, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,055 that established financial entities may give access to the Foreign Exchange Market
for the cancellation in the country or abroad of principal and interest of debt securities denominated in foreign currency, as long as such securities have been fully subscribed abroad and the funds obtained have been settled in the Foreign Exchange
Market. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;4, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,059 by means of which the requirement of prior conformity by the BCRA is
eliminated to make payments through the Foreign Exchange Market to foreign related counterparties for the following concepts: (i)&nbsp;interests on commercial debts for the import of goods and services whose maturity date are from July&nbsp;5,2024;
(ii) interest on other commercial debts; and (iii)&nbsp;interest on financial indebtedness. In (ii)&nbsp;and (iii) above, access to the Foreign Exchange Market must comply with certain requirements set forth in the aforementioned Communication. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;19, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,108 which it establishes new requirements for the access to the Foreign Exchange
Market: (i)&nbsp;it reduces the term from 180 days to 90 days for transactions with securities issued under foreign legislation; (ii)&nbsp;it allows the transfer of securities to foreign entities for the purpose of participating in a process of
repurchase of debt securities; and (iii)&nbsp;it allows access to the Foreign Exchange Market to acquire from a foreign investor equity interests in resident companies when the applicable regulatory requirements set forth in the aforementioned
Communication. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;3, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,112 establishing dispositions for the refinancing, repurchase
or redemption of debt, enabling payments in foreign currency of premiums, interest and expenses through the Foreign Exchange Market when certain requirements set forth in such Communication are met. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;17, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,118 reducing the term for access to the Foreign Exchange Market to 30 calendar
days for the payment of imports of goods that do not have a particular treatment previously determined. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;31, 2024, the BCRA issued
Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,122 allowing immediate access to the Foreign Exchange Market for the payment of freight for export operations under the conditions established in said Communication. It should be mentioned that, prior to this
Communication, it was necessary to wait 30 calendar days from the arrival of the goods at destination to make such payment to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.i) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress rejected the Decree
No.&nbsp;70/2023, and, as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, is pending to be considered by the Chamber of Deputies of the National Congress. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35.j) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742 (&#147;Bases Law&#148;) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;8, 2024, the Bases Law was published in the BO, which introduces several amendments to the Argentine legal framework including, among others:
(i)&nbsp;the declaration of emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters for a term of 1 year; (ii)&nbsp;the administrative reorganization of the National State; (iii)&nbsp;the privatization of certain companies and
corporations wholly or majority owned by the State; (iv)&nbsp;amendments to the Administrative Procedures Law No.&nbsp;19,549; (v) amendments in the energy and oil and gas matters (see Notes 35.a.1) and 35.c.1)); (vi) the creation of the RIGI to
encourage large investments with tax, customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights (see Note 35.e)); and (vii)&nbsp;a labor and union reform. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, the Group has entered into certain financing and insurance transactions with entities
related to the national public sector. Such transactions consist of certain financial transactions that are described in Notes 15, 16 and 22 and transactions with Naci&oacute;n Seguros S.A. related to certain insurance policies contracts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On the other hand, the Group holds Bonds of the Argentine Republic 2029, 2030 and 2038, BCRA bonds, and bonds issued by the National Government identified
as investments in financial assets (see Note 15). Additionally, the Group holds BCRA bills identified as cash and cash equivalents (see Note 16). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Furthermore, YPF has an indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest in Compa&ntilde;&iacute;a de Hidrocarburo No
Convencional S.R.L. (&#147;CHNC&#148;). During the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, YPF and CHNC carried out transactions, among others, the purchases of crude oil by YPF for 368 and 358, respectively. These transactions
were consummated in accordance with the general and regulatory conditions of the market. The net balance payable to CHNC as of September&nbsp;30, 2024 and December&nbsp;31, 2023 amounts to 84 and 38, respectively. See Note 36 to the annual
consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On May&nbsp;8, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;58/2024 was published in the BO, which establishes an exceptional,
transitory and unique payment regime for the balance of the MEM&#146;s economic transactions of December 2023, January 2024 and February 2024 corresponding to the MEM&#146;s creditors, and instructs CAMMESA to determine the amounts owed to each of
them corresponding to such economic transactions, to be cancelled as follows: (i)&nbsp;the economic transactions of December 2023 and January 2024, through the delivery of government securities denominated &#147;Bonos de la Rep&uacute;blica
Argentina en D&oacute;lares Estadounidenses Step Up 2038&#148;; and (ii)&nbsp;the economic transactions of February 2024, with the funds available in the bank accounts enabled in CAMMESA for collection purposes and with those funds available from
the transfers made by the National Goverment to the &#147;Fondo Unificado con Destino al Fondo de Estabilizaci&oacute;n&#148;. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of
September&nbsp;30, 2024, as mentioned above, the Group has recognized a charge for doubtful sales receivables of 40 in the &#147;Selling expenses&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 2.b.7) to the annual consolidated
financial statements), and in relation to our joint ventures YPF EE and CT Barrag&aacute;n a charge for such concept of 26 and 8, respectively, in the &#147;Income from equity interests in associates and joint ventures&#147; line item in the
statement of comprehensive income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The table below discloses the accrued compensation for the YPF&#146;s key management personnel, including members

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36. BALANCES AND TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, the Company performed an external benchmark analysis of the Board of Directors&#146; fees
and compensation of first-line executives. The conclusions were presented to the Compensation and Nomination Committee and, as a result, the components of the total compensation package were aligned with YPF&#146;s strategic plan and market
standards for local and international listed companies of similar magnitude. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As detailed in Note 37, a &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148; applicable
to eligible members of YPF&#146;s Management and a variable compensation based on results (&#147;CVR&#148;) which applies to 100% of the Company&#146;s employees, with the exception of the President and CEO and commercial agents, were implemented.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item1toc910119_43"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and
similar obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 3 and 2 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Performance bonus programs</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These programs
cover certain of the Group&#146;s personnel and are paid in cash. These bonuses are mainly based on compliance with VPs and related management objectives. They are calculated considering the annual compensation of each employee and certain key
factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives. As of 2024, a new variable bonus program based on corporate results (&#147;CVR&#148;) was implemented. This will be paid based on the Group&#146;s net profit before income tax, if it is
positive. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the performance bonus programs was 165 and 78 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30,
2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the Company adopted the &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of management of
YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights (&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants
comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the Company over a specified period of time. The
amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The PSARs expire five years after their grant and
begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US$ 30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common
share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share, resulting in a weighted average fair value of
US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer) which advised on its design and implementation.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 9.89 per PSARs.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">PSARs expense is determined based on the grant-date fair value of the awards. Fair value is calculated using Monte Carlo simulation model, which
requires the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the fair value of the Company&#146;s shares, expected term and risk-free interest rate. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with Value generation Plan was 7, for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remainder of the share-based plans was 5 and 2 to be settled in equity instruments, and 8 and 13 to be
settled in cash, for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 2.b) describes the accounting policies for
share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 31. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:20pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="right">HORACIO DANIEL MAR&Iacute;N </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_2"></A><U></U>LEGAL INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Legal address </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL">Macacha G&uuml;emes 515 - Ciudad Aut&oacute;noma de Buenos
Aires, Argentina. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Fiscal year </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL">No.&nbsp;48 beginning on January&nbsp;1,
2024. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Main business of the Company </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company&#146;s
purpose shall be to perform, on its own, through third parties or in association with third parties, the survey, exploration and exploitation of liquid and/or gaseous hydrocarbon fields and other minerals, as well as the industrialization,
transportation and commercialization of these products and their direct and indirect <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT> including petrochemical products, chemical products, whether derived from hydrocarbons or not, and <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-fossil</FONT> fuels, biofuels and their components, as well as the generation of electrical energy through the use of hydrocarbons, to which effect it may manufacture, use, purchase, sell, exchange, import or export
them. It shall also be the Company&#146;s purpose the rendering, on its own, through a controlled company or in association with third parties, of telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force after
applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well
as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its object. To better achieve these purposes, it may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or
private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Filing with the Public Registry of Commerce </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Bylaws filed on February&nbsp;5, 1991, under No.&nbsp;404, Book 108, Volume A, Sociedades An&oacute;nimas, with the Public Registry of Commerce of
Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, in charge of the Argentine Registry of Companies (Inspecci&oacute;n General de Justicia); and Bylaws in substitution of previous Bylaws, filed on June&nbsp;15, 1993, under No.&nbsp;5,109, Book 113, Volume A,

areas in Bolivia and sells jet fuel, natural gas, lubricants and derivatives in Chile and lubricants and derivatives in Brazil. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_8"></A>2. BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim consolidated financial statements of the Company for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are presented in
accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim financial reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2023 (&#147;annual consolidated financial
statements&#148;) presented in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Moreover, some additional information required by the LGS and/or
CNV&#146;s Rules have been included. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are unaudited. The Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the
nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.b)
Material accounting policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 18. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional and
presentation currency</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its
functional currency. Additionally, in accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV Rules, the Company must present its financial statements in pesos. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group maintains
share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 37 of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the
guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#147;Share-based payment&#148;. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service
based on the Group&#146;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#147;Share-based benefit plans&#148; account in the statement of
changes in shareholders&#146; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the grant conditions specified under the respective benefit plan.
