<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Cash-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service
based on the Group&#146;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest with an offsetting entry in the &#147;Salaries and social security&#148; line item in the statement of financial position, measured at fair value.
Changes in the fair value of the liability are recognized in net income in the statement of comprehensive income. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on
the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-market</FONT> vesting conditions. The impact of the revision of the original estimates, if applicable, is recognized in the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of September&nbsp;30, 2024, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and
interpretations issued by the IASB as of January</U><U></U><U>&nbsp;1, 2024, whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV Rules, the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for
issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 18 &#147;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1 &#147;Presentation of financial statements&#148;, with the objective of providing better
information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be grouped into 2 main groups: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Group income and expenses into 3 defined categories: (i)&nbsp;operating; (ii) financing and (iii)&nbsp;investing, and
include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Provide more information about the performance measures defined by management, which, although not mandatory, in the
event of including this type of measures, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to financial statements users, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the
statement of comprehensive income, among others. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize
information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the
application of IFRS 18. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>IFRS 19 &#147;Subsidiaries without public accountability: Disclosures&#148; </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 19 with the objective of allowing the option to apply simplified disclosure requirements in the financial statements of
subsidiaries without public accountability and with a parent company, ultimate or intermediate, that prepares consolidated financial statements for public use in accordance with IFRS. Its application is optional for fiscal years beginning on or
after January&nbsp;1, 2027. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:80pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2. &#8201;BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </B></P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and
liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of
preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key sources of uncertainty
about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed in Note
2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other information corresponding to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2023 and to the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2023 are an
integral part of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Likewise, changes have been made to the comparative figures in Notes 6 and 25 as mentioned in Note
5 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Note 6. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, from this fiscal year, the Group has made a change in the presentation of
the items in the &#147;Financial results, net&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 29). This change is intended to provide more relevant and detailed information on the origin of financial results and the effects of
transactions or conditions that affect the financial situation, financial performance, and cash flows of the Group such as interests and exchange differences generated by loans, among others; and improve the comparability of the Group&#146;s
financial statements with its peers. The comparative information for the nine and three-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2023 has been restated. &#147;Financial income&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income decreased by
561,806 and 288,907, for the nine and three-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2023, respectively; &#147;Financial costs&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income decreased by 398,713 and 188,197, for the nine and three-month
periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2023, respectively; and &#147;Other financial results&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income increased by 163,093 and 100,710, for the nine and three-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2023,
respectively. This change had no effect on the Group&#146;s statements of financial position, statements of changes in shareholders&#146; equity, statements of cash flows, Net financial results and net profit or loss. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_9"></A>3. SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_10"></A>4. ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Dissolution of the company YPF International</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
May&nbsp;6, 2024, the Plurinational Service of Registry of Commerce (&#147;SEPREC&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) of Bolivia approved the dissolution and liquidation of YPF International. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
credit risk and liquidity risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;29, 2024 the Court of Appeals confirmed the obligation to cease and remedy the environmental damage determined in the first instance. The <FONT

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_24"></A>18. INCOME TAX </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">According to IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of
the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the
income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to such tax criteria, the income tax expense contemplates the
application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the projected tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all
considering that the assumption of confiscation would be verified in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group considers having strong arguments to successfully defend such assumed tax criteria, in the event of a possible controversy with the tax
authorities, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 &#147;Uncertainty over income tax treatments&#148;. As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generates a profit of 365,505. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The income tax charge for the nine-month period ending September&nbsp;30, 2024 is a profit of 929,100. The amount accrued for the nine-month periods
ending September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023 is as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:11pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_37"></A>31. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,922 and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares
of common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of September&nbsp;30, 2024, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the
affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the
voluntary dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the
outstanding Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;26, 2024, the General
Shareholders&#146; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings:
(i)&nbsp;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of
1,003,419; (iii) allocate the amount of 28,745 to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 3,418,972 to constitute a reserve for investments. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P>

</TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>33. CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs and the Republic completed their briefing on the turnover motion on July&nbsp;8, 2024. The
District Court may, but is not required to, hold oral argument prior to rendering a decision on the turnover motion. Furthermore, the District Court&#146;s decision on the turnover motion may be appealed by Plaintiffs or the Republic in accordance
with applicable procedural rules. YPF is not a party to the turnover motion. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Plaintiffs are also seeking discovery of documents from YPF related to
their theory that YPF could be an &#147;alter ego&#148; of the Republic. YPF denies that it is an <I>alter ego</I> and objected to Plaintiffs&#146; document requests. On May&nbsp;28, 2024, the District Court ordered YPF to produce documents in
response to Plaintiffs&#146; discovery requests. To date, Plaintiffs have not requested that the District Court find that YPF is an <I>alter ego</I> of the Republic, and the District Court&#146;s order on discovery is not a ruling accepting
Plaintiffs&#146; <I>alter ego</I> theory. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;12, 2024, YPF filed a brief requesting that the District Court permanently enjoin Plaintiffs
from pursuing recovery from YPF in connection with their September&nbsp;15, 2023 final judgment against the Republic, arguing that Plaintiffs&#146; alter ego theory is barred under the doctrine of res judicata. Plaintiffs filed their opposition and
YPF filed its reply. On August&nbsp;29, 2024, the District Court adjourned the oral argument initially scheduled for September&nbsp;3, 2024, without setting a new date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF will continue to defend itself in accordance with the applicable legal procedures and available defenses. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company will continue to reassess the status of the litigation and its possible impact on the results and financial situation of the Group, as needed.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_40"></A>34. CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>34.a) Exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant agreements, exploitation concessions, transport concessions and exploration permits that took place in the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2023 are described in Note 34.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements. During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>34.b) Investment agreements and commitments and assignments </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant investment agreements and commitments and assignments are described in Note 34.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements.
Updates for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Andes Project</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In August and September 2024 YPF signed assignment agreements for 9 asset groups (25 conventional areas), subject to the fulfillment of closing
conditions including applicable regulatory and provincial approvals. The Company continues to develop the process of assignment or reversion of the remaining assets available for sale, as well as compliance with the closing conditions indicated
above. Considering the elements of judgment available at such date, the Company expects to comply with the plan within the terms and conditions duly approved by the Board of Directors of the Company on February&nbsp;29, 2024. See Note 9. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;29, 2024, Decree No.&nbsp;1,509/2024 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Chubut, authorizing the assignment of 100%
of YPF&#146;s rights in the &#147;Escalante - El Tr&eacute;bol&#148; exploitation concession in favor of PECOM SERVICIOS ENERGIA S.A.U. (&#147;PECOM&#148;) and subjecting the extension of such concession to the fulfillment of certain conditions by
YPF and by PECOM. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_41"></A>35. MAIN REGULATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.a.1) Hydrocarbons Law </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Hydrocarbons Law, as described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that international trade of hydrocarbons will be free, according to the terms and conditions established by
the PEN. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that exploration permit holders and/or exploitation concessionaires, refiners and/or marketers may freely
export hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives, subject to the SE&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-objection.</FONT> The effective exercise of this right will be subject to regulations issued by the PEN, which, among other aspects, must
consider: (i)&nbsp;the usual requirements related to the access to technically proven resources; and (ii)&nbsp;that the eventual objection of the SE may only be formulated within 30 days of being informed of the exports to be made, and must be based
on technical or economic reasons related to the security of supply. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Incorporates hydrocarbon processing and natural gas storage activities, for which the national or provincial Executive
Branch, as applicable, may grant storage and/or processing authorizations. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Changes the legal figure of &#147;transport concession&#148; to the figure of &#147;transport authorization&#148;.
</P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes that exploitation concessions and transportation concessions granted prior to the enactment of the Base Law
will continue to be governed until their expiration by the legal framework existing at the date of approval of the Bases Law. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Determines that in exploitation concession bidding processes the royalties to be paid to the application authority will
be offered by the concessionaire, determining that the royalty to be offered will be 15% plus or minus a percentage to be chosen by the bidder. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Other modifications establish that: (i)&nbsp;the request for conversion of a conventional exploitation concession into
a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-conventional</FONT> exploitation concession will only be available until December&nbsp;31, 2028 and its term will be 35 years without extensions; (ii)&nbsp;for new exploitation concessions, the national or
provincial Executive Branch, as applicable, at the time of defining the terms and conditions of the bidding, may determine in a reasoned manner other terms of up to 10 years more than those provided for in the Hydrocarbons Law; (iii)&nbsp;owners of
projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction and/or any other hydrocarbon industrialization process may request an authorization to transport hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives to their
industrialization facilities and from the same to subsequent industrialization or commercialization process centers and/or facilities; (iv)&nbsp;those authorized to process hydrocarbons must process hydrocarbons from third parties up to a maximum of
5% of the capacity of their facilities; and (v)&nbsp;the fee for each square kilometer or fraction thereof that a holder of an exploration permit must pay annually and in advance shall be calculated according to a scale determined by the price of a
barrel of oil quoted on the &#147;Frontline ICE Brent&#148;. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.b) Regulations applicable to the Downstream business segment
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.b)
to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.c) Regulations applicable to the Gas and Power business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.c.1) Transportation, distribution and commercialization of natural gas </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Through the Bases Law (see Note 35.j)), amendments were incorporated in relation to the Gas Law, as described below: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">The PEN is entrusted with regulating natural gas exports following the same terms and conditions as for liquid
hydrocarbon exports as described in Note 35.a.1). </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="4%">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left">-</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Establishes a special regime for long-term firm export authorizations for liquefied natural gas. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">

reservoirs&#148;. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

request the renewal of their licenses for an additional <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">20-year</FONT> period. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify">Creates the &#147;Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas y la Electricidad&#148;, which will replace and assume the functions
of the &#147;Ente Nacional Regulador de la Electricidad&#148; (&#147;ENRE&#148;) and ENARGAS. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.c.2) Regulatory requirements
applicable to natural gas distribution </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;3, 2024, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;120/2024 was published in the BO, approving the transition tariff tables and rates and charges for
services to be applied by Metrogas as from such date, and the tariff update formula applicable on such transition tariff tables as from May 2024. On May&nbsp;27, 2024, the tariff updates corresponding to May, June and July 2024 were postponed by
instruction of the SE to ENARGAS, which generated an objection by Metrogas to such instructions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;6, 2024, ENARGAS Resolution
No.&nbsp;260/2024 was published in the BO, approving the transition tariff tables and rates and charges for services to be applied by Metrogas as from such date. See Note 35.d). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On November&nbsp;4, 2024, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;737/2024 was published in the BO, approving the transition tariff charts to be applied by Metrogas
to the consumption made as from the date. See Note 35.d). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These transition measures will remain in force until the rates resulting from the RTI come
into force, in accordance with the provisions of Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.d) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.d) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Plan for Reinsurance and Promotion of Federal Hydrocarbon Production Domestic Self-Sufficiency,
Exports, Imports Substitution and the Expansion of the Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#147;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#148;)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;27, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;41/2024 was published in the BO, which approved natural gas prices at the PIST in U.S. dollars
corresponding to the awarded volumes entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 which will be applicable for natural gas consumptions made: (i)&nbsp;from April&nbsp;1 and until April&nbsp;30, 2024; (ii) from May&nbsp;1 and until
September&nbsp;30, 2024; and (iii)&nbsp;from October&nbsp;1 and until December&nbsp;31, 2024; and instructed that, for the purpose of transferring the prices of natural gas to the tariff schemes of the public service of distribution of natural gas,
ENARGAS issue the tariff schemes that reflect on a monthly basis the variation of the exchange rate of the prices of natural gas to be transferred to the tariff schemes<B>.</B> </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On August&nbsp;19, 2024, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;216/2024 was published in the BO, which resolved to eliminate the maximum prices applicable set for
bottled LPG for residential use and replace them with a reference price system (without ceiling). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.e) Investment incentive programs </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Large Investment Incentive Regime (&#147;RIGI&#148;)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Bases Law (see Note 35.j)) created the RIGI, regulated by Decree No.&nbsp;749/2024 published in the BO on August&nbsp;23, 2024, General Resolution
No.&nbsp;1,074/2024 of the Ministry of Economy published in the BO on October&nbsp;22, 2024 and AFIP General Resolution No.&nbsp;5,590/2024 published in the BO on October&nbsp;23, 2024, which is intended to encourage large investments with tax,
customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights. This regime seeks to encourage investments, promote economic development, create employment and strengthen local production chains. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The RIGI is aimed at investment projects in the forestry industry, tourism, infrastructure, mining, technology, iron and steel, energy and oil and gas
sectors, with a minimum investment per sector or subsector or productive stage equal to or greater than a range between US$ 200,000,000 up to US$ 900,000,000 in computable assets, as established by the application authority. Interested parties have
2 years to adhere to the RIGI, submitting and obtaining the approval of an investment plan by the application authority. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The benefits of the RIGI
include a 25% income tax rate, accelerated amortization of investments, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-expirable</FONT> tax loss carryforwards, indexing tax losses by the Internal Wholesale Price Index (&#147;IPIM&#148;) published by the
INDEC, and exemptions from import and export duties, among others. In addition, foreign exchange incentives are established, such as the free availability of foreign currency on a staggered basis obtained from exports and certain flexibility related
to financing. The RIGI guarantees tax, customs and foreign exchange regulatory stability for 30 years from accession, protecting investment projects from more burdensome legislative changes. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.f) Tax regulations </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the
regulatory framework described in Note 35.e) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Tax for an Inclusive and Solidary Argentina (&#147;PAIS Tax&#148;, by its acronym in Spanish)</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;2, 2024, Decree No.&nbsp;777/2024 was published in the BO, which reduced to 7.5% the rate applied to foreign currency purchases for
contracting, abroad or in the country by <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-residents,</FONT> freight services and other transport services for the import or export of goods and for the import of goods, except for those mentioned in section 2
paragraph e) of Decree No.&nbsp;377/2023 and its corresponding regulations. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.g) Custom regulations </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.h) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 35.g) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the nine-month period ended
September&nbsp;30, 2024, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;18, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 7,994 which allows the possibility
of applying the collection of exports to the payment of capital and interest on financial debts abroad that are settled in the Foreign Exchange Market from April&nbsp;19, 2024 and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the average
life of the debt is not less than 3 years; and (ii)&nbsp;the first capital payment is not made before the year it was entered and settled in the Foreign Exchange Market; and established the possibility of not filing for the BCRA&#146;s prior
approval process more than 3 days before the maturity of the capital and interest for access to the Foreign Exchange Market when debt payments abroad are anticipated and as long as the following conditions are met: (i)&nbsp;the access occurs
simultaneously with the settlement of a new financial debt granted by a local financial entity from a line of credit from abroad as of April&nbsp;19, 2024; (ii) the average life of the new debt is greater than the average remaining life of the
anticipated debt; and (iii)&nbsp;the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the new indebtedness does not exceed the accumulated amount of principal maturities of the anticipated debt. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On June&nbsp;28, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,055 that established financial entities may give access to the Foreign Exchange Market
for the cancellation in the country or abroad of principal and interest of debt securities denominated in foreign currency, as long as such securities have been fully subscribed abroad and the funds obtained have been settled in the Foreign Exchange
Market. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;4, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,059 by means of which the requirement of prior conformity by the BCRA is
eliminated to make payments through the Foreign Exchange Market to foreign related counterparties for the following concepts: (i)&nbsp;interests on commercial debts for the import of goods and services whose maturity date are from July&nbsp;5,2024;
(ii) interest on other commercial debts; and (iii)&nbsp;interest on financial indebtedness. In (ii)&nbsp;and (iii) above, access to the Foreign Exchange Market must comply with certain requirements set forth in the aforementioned Communication. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On September&nbsp;19, 2024 the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,108 which it establishes new requirements for the access to the Foreign Exchange
Market: (i)&nbsp;it reduces the term from 180 days to 90 days for transactions with securities issued under foreign legislation; (ii)&nbsp;it allows the transfer of securities to foreign entities for the purpose of participating in a process of
repurchase of debt securities; and (iii)&nbsp;it allows access to the Foreign Exchange Market to acquire from a foreign investor equity interests in resident companies when the applicable regulatory requirements set forth in the aforementioned
Communication. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;3, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,112 establishing dispositions for the refinancing, repurchase
or redemption of debt, enabling payments in foreign currency of premiums, interest and expenses through the Foreign Exchange Market when certain requirements set forth in such Communication are met. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;17, 2024, the BCRA issued Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,118 reducing the term for access to the Foreign Exchange Market to 30 calendar
days for the payment of imports of goods that do not have a particular treatment previously determined. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On October&nbsp;31, 2024, the BCRA issued
Communication &#147;A&#148; 8,122 allowing immediate access to the Foreign Exchange Market for the payment of freight for export operations under the conditions established in said Communication. It should be mentioned that, prior to this
Communication, it was necessary to wait 30 calendar days from the arrival of the goods at destination to make such payment to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident.</FONT> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.i) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;14, 2024, the Chamber of Senators of the National Congress rejected the Decree

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.j) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742 (&#147;Bases Law&#148;) </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;8, 2024, the Bases Law was published in the BO, which introduces several amendments to the Argentine legal framework including, among others:
(i)&nbsp;the declaration of emergency in administrative, economic, financial and energy matters for a term of 1 year; (ii)&nbsp;the administrative reorganization of the National State; (iii)&nbsp;the privatization of certain companies and
corporations wholly or majority owned by the State; (iv)&nbsp;amendments to the Administrative Procedures Law No.&nbsp;19,549; (v) amendments in the energy and oil and gas matters (see Notes 35.a.1) and 35.c.1)); (vi) the creation of the RIGI to
encourage large investments with tax, customs and exchange benefits, guaranteeing legal certainty and the protection of acquired rights (see Note 35.e)); and (vii)&nbsp;a labor and union reform. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>35.k) CNV regulatory framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Information
requirements as Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial

not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the
jurisdiction of the CNV. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with the CNV Rules, the Company is subject to the provisions of Article 5 c), Chapter II, Title VII of the CNV

</TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36. BALANCES AND TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES (cont.) </B></P>
<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, the Company performed an external benchmark analysis of the Board of Directors&#146; fees
and compensation of first-line executives. The conclusions were presented to the Compensation and Nomination Committee and, as a result, the components of the total compensation package were aligned with YPF&#146;s strategic plan and market
standards for local and international listed companies of similar magnitude. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As detailed in Note 37, a &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148; applicable
to eligible members of YPF&#146;s Management and a variable compensation based on results (&#147;CVR&#148;) which applies to 100% of the Company&#146;s employees, with the exception of the President and CEO and commercial agents, were implemented.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="item2toc910119_43"></A>37. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and similar
obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 2,890 and 667 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023,
respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Performance bonus programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These programs cover certain of the Group&#146;s personnel and are paid in cash. These bonuses are mainly based on compliance with VPs and related
management objectives. They are calculated considering the annual compensation of each employee and certain key factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives. As of 2024, a new variable bonus program based on corporate results
(&#147;CVR&#148;) was implemented. This will be paid based on the Group&#146;s net profit before income tax, if it is positive. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to
expense related to the performance bonus programs was 152,788 and 31,284 for the nine-month periods ended September&nbsp;30, 2024 and 2023, respectively. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In April 2024, the
Company adopted the &#147;Value Generation Plan&#148;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. Under
this Plan, the Company granted 4.6&nbsp;million performance stock appreciation rights (&#147;PSARs&#148;) to plan participants comprising key employees of the Company. The PSARs provide beneficiaries the opportunity to receive an award to be settled
in cash equivalent to the appreciation in the value of the common shares of the Company over a specified period of time. The amount to be paid upon exercise is the difference between the per share base price determined by the plan and the per share
market value of the Company&#146;s common shares as of the exercise date. The PSARs expire five years after their grant and begin to vest in the third year, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditions, including performance milestones related
to the price of the Company&#146;s common shares ranging from a minimum of US$ 30 per common share up to US$ 60 per common share. The beneficiaries of the PSARs are also required to remain in the Company for three years from the granting of the
plan. The PSARs granted by the Company have a base price of US$ 16.17 per share, resulting in a weighted average fair value of US$ 8.75 per PSAR as of the granting date. The Value Generation Plan was approved by the Compensation and Nomination
Committee of the Company with the support of a management consulting firm (Mercer) which advised on its design and implementation. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:120pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
